title: C# Questions & Answers - Introduction of Console I/O Operations
sourceFile: C# Questions & Answers - Introduction of Console I_O Operations - Sanfoundry.html
description: This set of C# Questions and Answers focuses on "Introduction of Console I/O operations".

questions.question: Which of the classes provide the operation of reading from and writing to the console in C#.NET?
questions.explanation: The method for reading and writing to the console in C#.NET is provided by System.Console class. This class gives us access to the standard input, output and standard error streams.

questions.question: Which of the given stream methods provide access to the output console by default in C#.NET?
questions.explanation: The standard output stream Console.Out sends output to the screen by default.

questions.question: Which of the given stream methods provide access to the input console in C#.NET?
questions.explanation: Console.In is an instance of TextReader, and we can use the methods and properties defined by TextReader to access it to read the input from the keyboard.

questions.question: The number of input methods defined by the stream method Console.In in C#.NET is?
questions.explanation: Two basic methods : read() and readline() and third method readkey() introduced in .NET FrameWork 2.0.

questions.question: Select the correct methodS provided by Console.In?
questions.explanation: The two method Read() and ReadLine() available in .NET Framework 1.0 and Third method ReadKey() was added by .NET Framework 2.0.

questions.question: Choose the output returned when read() reads the character from the console?
questions.explanation: Read() returns the character read from the console. It returns the result. The character is returned as an int, which should be cast to char.

questions.question: Choose the output returned when an error condition is generated while read() reads from the console.
questions.explanation: Read() returns -1 on error. This method also throws an IOException on failure.

questions.question: Choose the object of TextReader class.
questions.explanation: Console.In is an instance(object) of TextReader class and we can use the methods and properties defined by TextReader to invoke the object console.in.

questions.question: Choose the object/objects defined by the Textwriter class.
questions.explanation: Console.Out and Console.Error are objects of type TextWriter class.
